evidence: The spectroscopic techniques such as XRF, SIMS and AAS after etching give information about the composition of the films, while structural information can be obtained with FTIR, XPS, EXAFS, XRD and AFM/STM. X-ray fluorescence (XRF) is a rapid and non-destructive method which after proper calibration can be used for the determination of the dopant concentrations and thicknesses of thin films. The Rutherford backscattering spectroscopy (RBS) technique allows quantitative and also non-destructive determination of the composition of thin film samples. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) is a convenient method for surface analysis since it does not destroy the sample and since no special measuring conditions such as ultrahigh vacuum are required.
